# “Almost Unlocked” Cocktails Filter (Missing One Ingredient)

**Labels:** P2 - Medium, Scope: MVP, Type: UX, Type: Enhancement

## Problem

The app currently answers:

> “What cocktails can I make?”

However, users often want to know:

> “What cocktails am I *one ingredient away* from making?”

These near-miss cocktails are useful for discovery and help guide users toward expanding their ingredient collection.

At the same time, showing locked cocktails in the main results list by default could clutter the experience.

---

## Feature Concept

Introduce an **“Almost Unlocked”** filter that shows cocktails that are **missing exactly one ingredient** from the user's ingredient list.

This feature should integrate with the upcoming **Advanced Filters system** rather than appearing by default in the main list.

Example:
Advanced Filters

☐ Almost Unlocked (Missing One Ingredient)


When enabled, the results list shows cocktails that are one ingredient away.

Example display:
```

Negroni
Missing: Campari

You have:
✓ Gin
✓ Sweet Vermouth
✗ Campari
```
---

## UX Goals

- Encourage discovery of new cocktails
- Show users how close they are to unlocking additional recipes
- Keep the main cocktail list clean and focused
- Integrate naturally with the Advanced Filters UI

---

## Functional Requirements

For the user's ingredient list:

1. Evaluate all cocktails not currently makeable.
2. Identify cocktails where:
   - exactly one ingredient is missing
3. Allow users to filter the cocktail list to show these results.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add **Almost Unlocked** option to Advanced Filters.
- Filter returns cocktails missing exactly **one ingredient**.
- Missing ingredient is clearly displayed in the cocktail card or detail view.
- Feature works alongside existing filters:
  - ingredient filters
  - search
  - time period
  - source
- If the filter is not enabled, these cocktails do **not** appear in the normal results list.

---

## Implementation Notes

- Reuse the existing ingredient-matching logic used by **You Can Make**.
- Compute missing ingredient count during match evaluation.
- Filter condition:
title: “Almost Unlocked” Cocktails Filter (Missing One Ingredient)

**Labels:** P1 - High, Scope: MVP, Type: UX, Type: Enhancement

## Problem

The Import/Export page already supports exporting JSON.  
Import currently requires manual friction:
- open JSON file in editor
- copy
- switch to app
- paste into Import textbox

This is annoying and error-prone.

## Request

Add a button that allows selecting a local JSON file and automatically populates the Import textbox with its contents.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a button near the Import textbox: **Load from File** (or similar)
- Clicking the button opens a file picker restricted to `.json` (or `application/json`)
- After choosing a file:
  - the file is read client-side
  - the Import textbox is filled with the file contents
- If file content is not valid JSON:
  - show a user-friendly error message
  - do not overwrite the existing Import textbox contents (or prompt)
- Support reasonably large JSON payloads (at least typical export size)
- No server upload is required (client-side read is fine)

## Implementation Notes (Vue)

- Use an `<input type="file" accept=".json,application/json" hidden>` triggered by the button
- Use `FileReader` to read text and set the bound model for the Import textbox
- Optional: validate with `JSON.parse` before setting (or validate after setting with error handling)
title: Import/Export: Add "Load JSON from File" Button for Import Box

body:
## Overview

We need an **Advanced Filters** UI pattern similar to shopping sites
(Amazon sidebar), but **collapsed by default** so the main page stays
clean.

The existing basic filters on the main page are correct and should
**NOT** be expanded further. Any additional filtering logic belongs in
this advanced pane.

This ticket defines both the **UI pattern** and the **filter
architecture** required to support future filtering features without
creating technical debt.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# MVP Goals

-   Add an **Advanced Filters pane**
-   Pane **slides in from the left**
-   Pane is **collapsed by default**
-   Main cocktail list remains visually uncluttered
-   Provide a **Reset All Filters** action

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# UI / UX Requirements

## Entry Point

-   Add an **Advanced Filters** button near existing filter controls
-   Clicking opens a **left-side drawer**
-   Drawer may overlay or push content depending on layout

## Pane Behavior

-   Closed by default
-   Slides in from the **LEFT**
-   Closing the pane **does not clear filters**
-   Works well on **mobile and desktop**

## Reset Behavior

Include a **Reset All Filters** action inside the pane.

Reset must:

-   Clear **ALL filters** (basic + advanced)
-   Restore global defaults
-   Immediately refresh results

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Advanced Filter Groups

The pane will contain these filter groups:

-   **My**
    -   My Submissions
    -   My Approved
-   **Cocktail Time Period**
-   **Source**
-   **Flavor Profile**
-   **Ingredients**

Ingredient filter behavior:

-   Show top \~15 popular ingredients initially
-   Provide **"See More" expansion**
-   Expansion should be **inline (Amazon style)**

Notes:

-   Ingredient list must remain performant
-   Avoid rendering very large checkbox lists
-   Must integrate with centralized filter pipeline

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Acceptance Criteria

-   Advanced Filters button opens a left drawer
-   Drawer closed by default
-   Reset clears all filters
-   Filter groups render correctly
-   Works on mobile + desktop
-   Main cocktail list remains uncluttered

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Filter Architecture

To ensure maintainability, filtering must follow a **centralized
pipeline architecture**.

This prevents logic from being scattered across components and ensures
counts and results always remain consistent.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Core Design Principles

### Single Source of Truth

The list rendered in the UI is the canonical filtered result.

All counts derive from this list.

Example:

``` vue
v-for="cocktail in displayedCocktails"
```

Count example:

    SHOWING = displayedCocktails.length

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Composable Filters

Each filter should be implemented as a pure function:

``` ts
(cocktail) => boolean
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### UI-Agnostic Logic

-   Advanced Filters only modify filter state
-   Filtering logic must not live in UI components

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Centralized Filter Pipeline

Filtering occurs in one computed pipeline.

Example:

``` ts
const displayedCocktails = computed(() => {
  let results = evaluatedCocktails

  results = results.filter(modeFilter)
  results = results.filter(searchFilter)
  results = results.filter(timePeriodFilter)
  results = results.filter(sourceFilter)
  results = results.filter(flavorProfileFilter)
  results = results.filter(ingredientFilter)

  return results
})
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Data Flow

## Base Dataset

    baseCocktails

This dataset is never mutated.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Filter State

``` ts
filterState = {
  mode: "CAN_MAKE" | "SHOW_ALL" | "ALMOST_UNLOCKED",
  searchText: "",
  selectedTimePeriods: [],
  selectedSources: [],
  selectedFlavorProfiles: [],
  selectedIngredients: [],
  includeUnapproved: false
}
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Ingredient Evaluation Metadata

Ingredient matching should be computed **once per cocktail**.

Example structure:

``` ts
{
  cocktail,
  ingredientIds: number[],
  canMake: boolean,
  missingCount: number,
  missingIngredientIds: number[]
}
```

This allows fast filtering for:

-   Can Make
-   Almost Unlocked
-   Missing ingredient logic

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Filter Mode Design

Use a single mode value instead of multiple booleans.

    CAN_MAKE
    SHOW_ALL
    ALMOST_UNLOCKED

This prevents impossible states such as:

-   canMake + showAll simultaneously active
-   almostUnlocked + canMake simultaneously active

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Additional Filter: Almost Unlocked

The **Almost Unlocked** filter identifies cocktails that are **missing
exactly one ingredient**.

This encourages discovery without cluttering the main UI.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Filter Definition

``` ts
missingCount === 1
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## UX Behavior

The filter appears inside **Advanced Filters** and is **disabled by
default**.

Example:

    ☐ Almost Unlocked (Missing One Ingredient)

Optional UI enhancement:

    Negroni
    Missing: Campari

    You have:
    ✓ Gin
    ✓ Sweet Vermouth
    ✗ Campari

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Ingredient Filter Performance

Ingredient filtering must use **IDs and Sets**, not string comparisons.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Problem to Avoid

Avoid patterns like:

    selectedIngredients.includes(name)

or repeated string comparisons inside filters.

These become slow as the dataset grows.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Recommended Implementation

### Store Selected Ingredients as IDs

``` ts
selectedIngredientIds: Set<number>
```

Membership checks become **O(1)**.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Precompute Cocktail Ingredient IDs

Each cocktail stores canonical ingredient IDs:

``` ts
ingredientIds: number[]
```

Optional:

``` ts
ingredientIdSet: Set<number>
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Ingredient Matching Example

``` ts
const canMake = ingredientIds.every(id =>
  userIngredientSet.has(id)
)
```

Missing ingredient evaluation:

``` ts
const missing = ingredientIds.filter(id =>
  !userIngredientSet.has(id)
)

const missingCount = missing.length
```

This powers:

-   Can Make
-   Almost Unlocked
-   Future filters

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Suggested Evaluated Cocktail Structure

``` ts
{
  cocktail,
  ingredientIds: number[],
  canMake: boolean,
  missingCount: number,
  missingIngredientIds: number[]
}
```

Filtering then becomes simple property checks.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# UI Performance Guidance

Ingredient filter panels can slow down due to **DOM size** rather than
computation.

Recommended UI patterns:

-   Ingredient **typeahead search**
-   Selected ingredients shown as **chips**

This minimizes rendered DOM nodes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Benefits

This architecture:

-   Prevents duplicated filter logic
-   Guarantees consistent counts
-   Keeps filtering fast
-   Makes new filters trivial to add
-   Works well with Codex-driven development

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Future Enhancements

Potential extensions:

-   Missing Two Ingredients
-   Unlock X Cocktails if You Buy This Bottle
-   Bar Expansion Suggestions
-   Integration with **What Should I Buy Next**
title: Advanced Filters Pane (Architecture + UX) with Reset All

GROUPING FOR:

- Favorites
- Party lists
- Thematic lists
- etc

So right now there was already an idea for "linking" the same drinks from different sources.  These recipes will almost always be different.  So you have 2 Gin and Tonics, one from source 1 and another from source 2.  So, this would allow for the display of multiple recipes of the same type (either on the same page or maybe with tabs) and you could also filter by this.

But it occurred to me that it would be nice to group cocktails together for any reason.  You should be able to create your own groupings like "Favorites" or "Rye Whiskey Only" or "2026 Superbowl Party" (drinks you will be making at the party).  

Of course needs to be easy to add recipes to groups and then view or filter by them.
title: Cocktail Grouping Strategy
